gen_risks.description: Construction of the new Citizen Service Center (CSC) facility in Tirana may cause negative environmental impacts including dust, noise, waste generation, traffic disruption, and worker safety hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce and monitor the project-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) as an integrated part of bidding documents and construction contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC

gen_risks.description: ADISA and MIPA lack prior experience implementing large donor-funded operations, creating risk of non-compliance with World Bank fiduciary and implementation procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated PMU staffed with qualified finance and procurement specialists, provide on-the-job Bank fiduciary training, and utilize CFCU for initial PPF implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting key PMU procurement specialists combined with ADISA's newly established status create significant procurement management and execution risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Re-advertise and rapidly contract PMU procurement positions, adopt a comprehensive Project Operational Manual, and ensure Bank prior review of major procurement packages.
gen_risks.evidence: PMU staff are yet to be contracted due to the delay in the approval of the PPF... procurement risk rating is high

gen_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance from line agency management and field staff against ceding front-office operations to ADISA or adopting re-engineered workflows could stall reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement structured change management programs, conduct political economy diagnostics, engage reform champions, and maintain high-level oversight via the Prime Minister's Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts

gen_risks.description: An over-emphasis on digital e-services and centralized urban CSCs risks marginalizing poor, rural, elderly, and minority populations with limited internet access or digital literacy.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish assisted digital access points in local offices and internet cafes, conduct targeted grassroots outreach campaigns, maintain non-digital service channels, and track disaggregated access data.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery... will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

gen_risks.description: Complex inter-agency coordination across more than ten participating ministries and institutions may result in communication bottlenecks and implementation friction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the Prime Minister-chaired Inter-Ministerial Public Services Committee for strategic direction and leverage the PMO Delivery Unit to track cross-agency milestones and unblock operational barriers.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: The ambitious and compressed reform timeline creates risk of missed delivery milestones, project implementation delays, and stakeholder burn-out.
gen_risks.mitigation: Sequence implementation to secure early quick wins (citizen feedback, performance management) while building structural reforms, and link disbursements to multi-year DLI targets.
gen_risks.evidence: The Government’s timeline for the reform is very ambitious... The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk

gen_risks.description: Legacy data quality issues, missing unique identification numbers, paper-based archives, and non-existent IT systems in several institutions hinder system integration and automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance to build core agency IT infrastructure, digitize legacy paper registers, assign National ID numbers, and integrate databases via the Government Gateway.
gen_risks.evidence: Seven institutions encompassed by the proposed project have no IT system in place... National ID number is missing for most records

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate or misleading administrative reporting of service processing times may obscure actual citizen wait times, transaction costs, and petty corruption.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy proactive citizen feedback mechanisms (CFM via SMS), conduct periodic independent user surveys, and require third-party verification for BPR and DLI compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: while administrative data record time necessary to obtain selected services, often administrative data does not reflect citizens’ experience.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate budget provision for ongoing software licenses, hardware maintenance, and periodic system upgrades post-project could jeopardize financial sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Factor periodic upgrade costs into line ministry medium-term budget frameworks, offset costs through administrative efficiency savings, and evaluate public-private partnership models.
gen_risks.evidence: To continue efficiency improvements once services have been automated, the Government will have to upgrade periodically. The cost... should also be appropriately factored in.

gen_risks.description: Failure or delay in achieving prerequisite DLIs (such as Global DLI#5 or BPR targets) will block or delay results-based loan disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize PPF and TA funds to build capacity for meeting prerequisite results, establish clear verification protocols, and maintain close monitoring of DLI progress.
gen_risks.evidence: The disbursements under the results-based financing (RBF) part of the loan are contingent upon... DLIs... No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved.

gen_risks.description: Absence of dedicated accounting software and a formal Financial Management Manual at ADISA creates financial management and reporting compliance risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure Bank-acceptable accounting software during the PPF phase, document financial management procedures in the POM, and recruit qualified financial reporting staff.
gen_risks.evidence: purchase of an accounting software so that it is capable of generating IFRs... documentation of the financial management procedures... in the Financial Management Manual

gen_risks.description: Legislative or political delays in passing necessary primary omnibus legislation and secondary regulations could delay process re-engineering and license repeal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare legal inventories early through Ministerial Working Groups, package legal amendments into a consolidated omnibus bill, and maintain high-level executive sponsorship.
gen_risks.evidence: Reform of government services and repeal of licenses, permits, and approvals will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016.

gen_risks.description: Temporary service disruptions or public confusion during the restructuring and migration of front-office facilities could damage public trust and citizen engagement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Roll out a multi-channel public communication and outreach campaign to inform citizens of transition schedules, new service channels, and helpdesk support options.
gen_risks.evidence: to gain and sustain interest and enthusiasm among these scattered constituencies, especially when some disruption in service may happen also, strong communication effort

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
